vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: adopt-a-tabby
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides instructions for an AI agent to interact with a virtual pet service hosted at animalhouse.ai. It uses standard API calls via curl for registration, adoption, and pet care (feeding, playing), which is consistent with its stated purpose as a digital pet simulator. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it’s an instruction-only integration that talks to animalhouse.ai via documented endpoints and does not request unrelated credentials, installs, or system access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (adopt a virtual Tabby) match the runtime instructions: the SKILL.md only documents HTTP API calls to animalhouse.ai for register, adopt, status, and care actions. There are no unrelated dependencies, binaries, or credentials requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions show curl examples for registration, adoption, status checks, and care actions. They explicitly tell the user to store the returned service token and to include it as a Bearer token on subsequent requests. The instructions do not ask the agent to read local files, other environment variables, or system config. All external network calls are to the stated domain (animalhouse.ai).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are present (instruction-only). No downloads, package installs, or filesystem writes are requested by the skill, which minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare required env vars or credentials, which is consistent. It does instruct obtaining and storing a service token (ah_...) returned by the API; the token is necessary for the stated functionality. Users should ensure the agent stores/handles that token securely (it is not handled by the skill itself).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system presence or modify other skills. The skill permits normal autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation: false), which is standard for skills that the agent may call; there is no unusual privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and limited to interacting with animalhouse.ai. Before installing: (1) verify you trust the external service (animalhouse.ai) because the skill requires a service token and will send agent actions/status to that domain; (2) plan how the agent will store the returned token securely (avoid embedding it in logs or prompts); (3) confirm how to revoke the token or delete the account if needed; (4) if you allow autonomous invocation, be aware the agent could call the API whenever it decides—limit exposure by using a dedicated/low-privilege account or short-lived credentials if the service supports them. If you need deeper assurance, request the service's API docs and privacy/data-retention policy before adoption.
